title: Apriori Algorithm: Uncovering Hidden Patterns in Data Mining | Association Rules

cues.en: -: Hello and welcome back to the course on Machine Learning.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回到機器學習課程。

cues.en: Today we're talking about the intuition behind the Apriori algorithm.
cues.zh: 今天要談 Apriori 演算法背後的直覺概念。

cues.en: So let's get started.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: And we're gonna get started by talking about a story.
cues.zh: 先從一個故事開始。

cues.en: It's a somewhat legend of data science or a legend that is quite well known in data science.
cues.zh: 這算是資料科學界的傳奇，或者說是很有名的故事。

cues.en: You may have heard of this legend.
cues.zh: 你可能聽過。

cues.en: It's not a myth, it actually happened, but as you know things when they happen a long time ago and then time passes and the facts get distorted.
cues.zh: 它不是神話，確實發生過，但事情發生很久之後，隨著時間經過，細節可能會失真。

cues.en: But I'll tell you my story of this legend and it might not be exactly correct, but this is how I know about and how I've heard about it.
cues.zh: 我會講自己知道的版本，可能不完全正確，但這是我所了解、聽說的內容。

cues.en: So, what do you think the commonality is between these two products, Pampers or diapers, and beer?
cues.zh: 你覺得這兩種產品，幫寶適或尿布，以及啤酒，有什麼共通點？

cues.en: What do you think they have in common and why are they part of this urban legend now?
cues.zh: 它們有什麼關聯，為什麼現在成了這個都市傳說的一部分？

cues.en: Why are they part of this data science legend?
cues.zh: 為什麼成了資料科學傳奇的一部分？

cues.en: Well, as the story goes, a company, we are not going to name the company, but a company that is actually like a convenience store
cues.zh: 故事是這樣：某家公司，就不提名字了，一家類似便利商店的公司，

cues.en: did some analytics around the products that people are purchasing.
cues.zh: 分析了大家購買的產品。

cues.en: And so they were looking at what people are checking out with, what are the commonalities?
cues.zh: 他們查看顧客結帳時買了什麼，有哪些共通點。

cues.en: And they analyze thousands and thousands and thousands of transactions.
cues.zh: 分析了成千上萬筆交易。

cues.en: So thousands of people who actually checked out, if not tens of thousands.
cues.zh: 也就是數千位，甚至數萬位實際結帳的顧客。

cues.en: And they found a very interesting thing that very often during certain times of the day when people shop in the afternoon
cues.zh: 發現一件很有趣的事：一天的特定時段，傍晚購物時，

cues.en: between six and 9 p.m.
cues.zh: 也就是下午六點到晚上九點，

cues.en: people who buy diapers also buy beer.
cues.zh: 買尿布的人也會買啤酒。

cues.en: And it was out of the blue, completely out of the blue why these two products are completely not connected.
cues.zh: 這完全出乎意料，因為這兩種產品完全沒有關聯。

cues.en: Why would somebody buy beer when they're buying diapers or why buy diapers when they're buying beer.
cues.zh: 為什麼有人買尿布會買啤酒，或者買啤酒會買尿布？

cues.en: So that was the fact that they came across in the data and the explanation to this fact, one of the plausible explanations
cues.zh: 這是從資料發現的事實，其中一個合理的解釋，

cues.en: is that in the afternoons or in the evenings when the husband gets home and their, like him, the husband
cues.zh: 是下午或晚上丈夫回家後，丈夫

cues.en: and the wife are taking care of the their baby they sometimes find that they run out of diapers and who has to go pick up the diapers?
cues.zh: 和妻子一起照顧寶寶，有時發現尿布用完了，誰得去買？

cues.en: Well, the husband has to go pick up the diapers.
cues.zh: 丈夫得去買尿布。

cues.en: Or the wife sends the husband to go pick up the diapers and while he's picking up the diapers, 'cause it's already after hours after work, he also, he's already in the convenience store, he also picks up some beer, right?
cues.zh: 或者妻子叫丈夫去買尿布，而他去買時，因為已經下班，既然人在便利商店，就順便買些啤酒，對吧？

cues.en: And so that is a plausible explanation.
cues.zh: 這是一個合理的解釋。

cues.en: Might be the case, might not be the case, but it sounds pretty reasonable.
cues.zh: 可能是，也可能不是，但聽起來很合理。

cues.en: And based on that, so that's something that you can't really think of just by yourself, but that comes from the data.
cues.zh: 這些事情光靠自己不太容易想到，而是來自資料。

cues.en: And based on that you can decide how to to arrange products in your store.
cues.zh: 根據這點，就可以決定店內產品如何陳列。

cues.en: So some stores might decide to put these two products closer to entice people to buy a beer when they're buying diapers.
cues.zh: 有些商店可能把兩種產品擺近一點，吸引買尿布的人也買啤酒。

cues.en: But actually a lot of stores do the opposite.
cues.zh: 但其實很多商店會反過來做。

cues.en: There are a lot of stores separate beer and diapers, just like they try to separate and you'll probably notice this from your convenience store
cues.zh: 很多店會把啤酒和尿布分開，就像你可能注意到便利商店，

cues.en: that they try to separate bread and milk as far as possible.
cues.zh: 會盡量把麵包和牛奶擺得遠一點。

cues.en: Why? Because that way they already know that these two products are bought together.
cues.zh: 為什麼？因為已經知道這兩種產品常被一起購買。

cues.en: And so you actually have to walk through the whole store to pick up, you've picked up your bread, and then to get to the milk you have to get all the way through the whole store
cues.zh: 這樣你就得走遍整家店，拿了麵包後，要拿牛奶就得走過整間店，

cues.en: to the completely opposite corner of the store.
cues.zh: 到完全相反的角落。

cues.en: So as you're walking through the store, you see more other products and you're more likely to pick up an additional item that you weren't actually planning on buying when you got to the store in the first place.
cues.zh: 走過店裡時，會看到更多其他產品，更可能多拿一件原本進店時沒打算買的東西。

cues.en: So there's a lot of interesting marketing tactics that are used based on this data, but the question is how do you get to this data?
cues.zh: 根據這些資料，可以採用很多有意思的行銷策略，但問題是，怎麼取得這些資料？

cues.en: And one of the ways to get to it is the Apriori algorithm.
cues.zh: 其中一個方法就是 Apriori 演算法。

cues.en: So let's talk about Apriori in a bit more detail now.
cues.zh: 現在更詳細地談 Apriori。

cues.en: All right, so Apriori is about people who bought something also bought something else, or who watched something also watched something else, or who did something also did something else.
cues.zh: Apriori 處理的是：買了某樣東西的人，也買了其他東西；看了某個內容，也看其他內容；或做了某件事，也做另一件事。

cues.en: So it analyzes and this whole association rule learning part of the course is all about analyzing when things come in pairs
cues.zh: 它會分析，而本課整個關聯規則學習部分，也都在分析哪些事情會成對出現，

cues.en: or in triplicates or in...
cues.zh: 或三個一起出現，或者……

cues.en: Not in sequence, but they are combined together for some reason looking for those rules and those ways that this happens.
cues.zh: 不是按順序，而是因為某些原因一起發生，找出其中的規則與組合方式。

cues.en: All right, so let's have a look.
cues.zh: 來看看。

cues.en: For instance, movie recommendation, right?
cues.zh: 例如電影推薦，對吧？

cues.en: So you've got user IDs, you've got movies that the people liked, movie one, two, three, four, movie one and two for the second person, and so on.
cues.zh: 有使用者 ID，以及他們喜歡的電影；第一位喜歡電影一、二、三、四，第二位喜歡一、二，依此類推。

cues.en: And from here, just by looking at it, even without not knowing anything about association rule learning or the Apriori algorithm, you can already tell
cues.zh: 光是看這裡，即使完全不了解關聯規則學習或 Apriori 演算法，也能看出，

cues.en: that there are some potential rules that can come out of this, that for instance, everybody who watches movie one, not everybody, but it is likely that people who watch movie one, will...
cues.zh: 其中可能有些規則。例如每個看過電影一的人，不是每個，而是看過電影一的人，很可能……

cues.en: Or who like movie one, will also like movie number two.
cues.zh: 或者說，喜歡電影一的人，也會喜歡電影二。

cues.en: And people who like movie number two are quite likely to also like movie number four.
cues.zh: 喜歡電影二的人，很可能也喜歡電影四。

cues.en: And people who like movie number one are also quite likely to like movie number three.
cues.zh: 喜歡電影一的人，也很可能喜歡電影三。

cues.en: So there you can come up with lots of different potential rules, but some are gonna be stronger, some are gonna be weaker and we want to find the very strong ones in order to build our business decisions
cues.zh: 可以提出很多不同的潛在規則，但有些強、有些弱。我們想找非常強的規則，讓商業決策

cues.en: or our other decisions on those rules that we can see in the data, we don't have to go and ask people, "Hey, do you like movie number one?
cues.zh: 或其他決策有資料中的規則作依據，不用跑去問大家：「你喜歡電影一嗎？」

cues.en: "And would you like movie number two?
cues.zh: 「那你會喜歡電影二嗎？」

cues.en: "Because of that, do you like moving number two?"
cues.zh: 「因為這個原因，你喜歡電影二嗎？」

cues.en: Or, "What is your taste and preference?"
cues.zh: 或者問：「你的品味與偏好是什麼？」

cues.en: We can see these things from the data and we wanna extract this information and as long as we have a large enough sample size, if it's not just like five people, if it's 50,000 or 500,000 people that we're analyzing,
cues.zh: 這些都能從資料看出來，我們想擷取這些資訊；只要樣本夠大，不是只分析五人，而是五萬或五十萬人，

cues.en: we can come up with some quite solid rules.
cues.zh: 就能得到相當可靠的規則。

cues.en: All right, so here's another example where we've got a market basket.
cues.zh: 再看另一個例子，購物籃。

cues.en: So example of people who buy not just groceries, but this is more kind of like a a restaurant or a takeaway place.
cues.zh: 這不只是買雜貨的人，比較像餐廳或外帶店。

cues.en: And here you can see there's a link obviously, between burgers and french fries, interesting vegetables and fruits, and people are trying to be healthy, burgers french fries and ketchup.
cues.zh: 可以看到漢堡和薯條顯然有關聯；蔬菜與水果也很有趣，大家想吃得健康；還有漢堡、薯條與番茄醬。

cues.en: So again, these are potential rules, not necessarily the ones that we're gonna take away from data.
cues.zh: 這些只是可能的規則，不一定是最後會從資料採用的規則。

cues.en: This is just an example of something that you might observe visually just by looking at this data set.
cues.zh: 只是示範，光看這個資料集，可能就能觀察到什麼。

cues.en: All right, so how does the Apriori algorithm work?
cues.zh: Apriori 演算法如何運作？

cues.en: Well, the Apriori algorithm has three parts to it.
cues.zh: 它有三個部分。

cues.en: Its got the support, the confidence, and the lift.
cues.zh: 支持度、信賴度和提升度。

cues.en: So we're gonna start off with the support and you will see that it's very similar to something we've already discussed.
cues.zh: 先從支持度開始，你會發現和以前討論過的內容很像。

cues.en: It's very similar to the way we talked about the intuition for the Bayesian, for the naive Bayes classifiers.
cues.zh: 很像先前解釋貝氏、Naive Bayes 分類器的直覺概念。

cues.en: So let's have a look here, we've got movie recommendations.
cues.zh: 這裡以電影推薦為例。

cues.en: Support for movie M is...
cues.zh: 電影 M 的支持度是……

cues.en: The number is defined as a number of users who watched movie M divided by the total number of users.
cues.zh: 定義為看過電影 M 的使用者人數，除以使用者總人數。

cues.en: And market basket optimization, the same thing.
cues.zh: 購物籃最佳化也是一樣。

cues.en: Number of transactions containing certain item, I, divided by the total number of transactions.
cues.zh: 包含特定商品 I 的交易筆數，除以交易總筆數。

cues.en: Let's have a look at an illustration.
cues.zh: 看個圖示。

cues.en: Here we've got a hundred people, so we've got five rows and 20 columns of human beings.
cues.zh: 這裡有一百人，五列、二十欄的人。

cues.en: And let's see how many of them, let's say we're talking about a movie and I'm gonna give an example of one of my favorite movies "Ex Machina."
cues.zh: 假設談的是電影，就用我最喜歡的電影之一《人造意識》Ex Machina 當例子，看看有多少人看過。

cues.en: And if you haven't seen it, definitely check it out.
cues.zh: 如果還沒看過，一定要看看。

cues.en: It's all about AI and machine learning.
cues.zh: 內容和 AI、機器學習很有關。

cues.en: So let's say, let's see how many of these people have actually seen "Ex Machina?"
cues.zh: 來看這些人當中，有多少人看過《人造意識》？

cues.en: So there we go, there's 10 people who have seen "Ex Machina."
cues.zh: 有十人看過。

cues.en: Right, out of a hundred, so what does that mean?
cues.zh: 一百人中有十人，代表什麼？

cues.en: That means our support here is 10%.
cues.zh: 代表這裡的支持度是 10%。

cues.en: Good. Okay, now let's move on to step two.
cues.zh: 很好，進入第二步。

cues.en: Step two is we need to find the confidence.
cues.zh: 第二步要找信賴度。

cues.en: What is the confidence?
cues.zh: 什麼是信賴度？

cues.en: Well, confidence is defined as the number, let's go for movies, So the number of people who have seen movies, M1 and M2 divided
cues.zh: 以電影來說，信賴度定義為同時看過 M₁ 與 M₂ 兩部電影的人數，除以

cues.en: by the number of people have seen movie M1.
cues.zh: 看過電影 M₁ 的人數。

cues.en: So here we're going to assume that we're testing a rule, we're testing a rule that let's say people who have seen "Interstellar," where we have a hypothesis that says,
cues.zh: 假設正在測試一條規則，也就是看過《星際效應》的人，我們有個假設說，

cues.en: that people who have seen "Interstellar" they are also or have liked "Interstellar" are also likely to like "Ex Machina"
cues.zh: 看過，或喜歡《星際效應》的人，也很可能喜歡《人造意識》，

cues.en: or let's even go, who've seen...
cues.zh: 或者乾脆說，看過……

cues.en: People who have seen "Interstellar" are also likely to have seen "Ex Machina."
cues.zh: 看過《星際效應》的人，也很可能看過《人造意識》。

cues.en: So basically here, movie number one, M1 is going to be the "Interstellar" movie,
cues.zh: 基本上，這裡第一部電影 M₁ 是《星際效應》，

cues.en: the one that we're saying, "Okay, so we're gonna take everybody who's seen "Interstellar" and we're gonna check how many of them have seen "Ex Machina" and that's exactly what we're doing here.
cues.zh: 我們取出所有看過《星際效應》的人，檢查其中多少人看過《人造意識》，這正是現在要做的。

cues.en: And market basket optimization, same thing, you can think of an example of french fries and burgers.
cues.zh: 購物籃最佳化也一樣，可以想成薯條與漢堡的例子。

cues.en: For instance, people have had burgers, who've ordered burgers also likely to order french fries.
cues.zh: 例如點了漢堡的人，也很可能點薯條。

cues.en: So at the top you would have people have ordered burgers and french fries, and the at the bottom you'll have people who have ordered burgers only, well, who have ordered burgers
cues.zh: 分子是同時點漢堡和薯條的人，分母是只點漢堡的人，或者說，點過漢堡的人，

cues.en: regardless of whether they've ordered french fries or not.
cues.zh: 不論有沒有點薯條。

cues.en: Much easier to talk about this with an illustration.
cues.zh: 用圖示說明會容易得多。

cues.en: Let's say those people colored in green are the ones who have seen "Interstellar" who have watched this movie.
cues.zh: 假設綠色的人，就是看過《星際效應》的人。

cues.en: Now we want to know, not out of our whole population, but out of just those people who have seen "Interstellar" how many of them have seen "Ex Machina?"
cues.zh: 現在想知道的不是整體人口，而是只在看過《星際效應》的人裡面，有多少人看過《人造意識》？

cues.en: So out of them we have seven people who have also seen "Ex Machina."
cues.zh: 其中有七人也看過《人造意識》。

cues.en: So there's only seven people who have seen both movies.
cues.zh: 所以只有七人兩部都看過。

cues.en: That's what we're after.
cues.zh: 這就是我們想找的。

cues.en: And so our confidence is going to be seven divided by 40.
cues.zh: 信賴度就是 7 除以 40。

cues.en: Just by definition, this is how it's calculated, 40 people have seen "Interstellar" and seven people out of those 40 have actually also seen "Ex Machina."
cues.zh: 依照定義這樣計算：40 人看過《星際效應》，其中七人也看過《人造意識》。

cues.en: So the conference here is 17.5%, good.
cues.zh: 所以這裡的信賴度是 17.5%，很好。

cues.en: And the next part or the third and last step is the lift.
cues.zh: 接下來第三個，也是最後一個部分，是提升度。

cues.en: And what is the lift?
cues.zh: 什麼是提升度？

cues.en: Lift is very simple again, is gonna be very similar to what we had in the naive Bayes, naive Bayesian classifiers
cues.zh: 一樣很簡單，也會很像之前 Naive Bayes 分類器，

cues.en: in that algorithm when we were discussing it.
cues.zh: 也就是討論那個演算法時看過的內容。

cues.en: So the lift is basically the confidence divided by the support.
cues.zh: 提升度基本上就是信賴度除以支持度。

cues.en: So what we calculated in step two divided by what we calculated in step one, and let's just talk about it in the illustration, because it's gonna make way more sense that way.
cues.zh: 第二步算出的值，除以第一步算出的值。用圖示來談，會更容易理解。

cues.en: So here's our population, those people in green are the ones who have seen "Interstellar," and all of these people in red are the ones who have seen "Ex Machina."
cues.zh: 這是整體人口，綠色是看過《星際效應》的人，所有紅色的人是看過《人造意識》的人。

cues.en: So basically our lift is all right, so if we just randomly suggest to a person to watch "Ex Machina,"
cues.zh: 基本上，提升度是這樣：如果隨機向一個人推薦《人造意識》，

cues.en: what is the likelihood that it's a movie for them?
cues.zh: 這部電影適合他的可能性是多少？

cues.en: It's a movie that, not in this population, like out of the out of this population, we know that out of 100 people only 10 actually watch "Ex Machina" and we're going to assume
cues.zh: 在這個群體之外，我們知道這裡一百人中只有十人看過《人造意識》，而我們假設

cues.en: that watched and liked are interchangeable terms here.
cues.zh: 「看過」和「喜歡」在這裡可以互換。

cues.en: So we're going to assume that if they didn't watch it they're not gonna like it anyway.
cues.zh: 所以假設沒看過的人，反正也不會喜歡。

cues.en: So if we take another random population
cues.zh: 如果再取另一個隨機群體，

cues.en: and then what is the likelihood that if we recommend to a random person in that population that brand new population, we recommend that the "Ex Machina" movie,
cues.zh: 向這個全新群體中的一個隨機對象推薦《人造意識》，

cues.en: what is the likelihood that they will like it?
cues.zh: 他喜歡的機率是多少？

cues.en: Well, the likelihood is 10%, because out of a hundred people only 10 of them actually liked that movie.
cues.zh: 是 10%，因為一百人中只有十人喜歡這部電影。

cues.en: But now the question is, can we prove that result by using some prior knowledge?
cues.zh: 現在的問題是，能不能利用一些先驗知識，改善這個結果？

cues.en: That's why the algorithm is called Apriori.
cues.zh: 這就是演算法叫 Apriori 的原因。

cues.en: In that new population, let's only recommend "Ex Machina" to people who have already seen "Interstellar" to people who are marked as green in this population.
cues.zh: 在新群體中，只向已看過《星際效應》的人推薦《人造意識》，也就是對應這裡綠色的人。

cues.en: So we'll only ask, "Have you seen Interstellar?"
cues.zh: 只要問：「你看過《星際效應》嗎？」

cues.en: If they have, then we'll recommend "Ex Machina."
cues.zh: 如果看過，就推薦《人造意識》。

cues.en: What is the likelihood that a person will actually like "Ex Machina," if we recommend them that way?
cues.zh: 如果用這種方式推薦，對方真的喜歡《人造意識》的機率是多少？

cues.en: Well in that case, the likelihood as we've calculated out of the green people only, not only, out of the green people 17 and a half percent actually liked "Ex Machina."
cues.zh: 根據剛才的計算，綠色的人裡面有 17.5% 喜歡《人造意識》。

cues.en: So the lift is the improvement in your prediction.
cues.zh: 所以提升度代表預測的改善程度。

cues.en: So your your original prediction's 10%, if you just randomly take a person out of your new population and recommend "Ex Machina" they'll like it for the likelihood of 10%.
cues.zh: 原本的預測是 10%；如果從新群體隨機挑一人，推薦《人造意識》，他喜歡的機率是 10%。

cues.en: If you first ask the question, have you seen and liked "Interstellar?"
cues.zh: 如果先問：「你看過而且喜歡《星際效應》嗎？」

cues.en: If they say, yes, and then you recommend "Ex Machina" the likelihood of a successful recommendation there is 17.5%.
cues.zh: 他回答是，再推薦《人造意識》，成功推薦的機率就是 17.5%。

cues.en: So the lift is by definition 1.75.
cues.zh: 因此，依照定義，提升度是 1.75。

cues.en: There we go, that is what the lift is defined as.
cues.zh: 這就是提升度的定義。

cues.en: And that's pretty much the whole Apriori algorithm.
cues.zh: Apriori 演算法大致就是這樣。

cues.en: That's the steps that it involves.
cues.zh: 這些就是它的步驟。

cues.en: And now we're just going to put it all together in this one kind of step by step process.
cues.zh: 現在把它們整合成一個逐步流程。

cues.en: So step one, you need to set up a minimum support and confidence.
cues.zh: 第一步，設定最低支持度與最低信賴度。

cues.en: So you might want to only...
cues.zh: 你可能只想……

cues.en: Because there's so many different recommendations.
cues.zh: 因為有很多不同的推薦。

cues.en: We only looked at one example, one specific example to simplify things, we talked about "Ex Machina" and "Interstellar."
cues.zh: 為了簡化，剛才只看一個特定例子，也就是《人造意識》和《星際效應》。

cues.en: But as you could see in the examples before that you could have like a hundred different movies and the different combinations, like Apriori is actually quite a slow algorithm,
cues.zh: 但從先前例子可以看到，可能有一百部不同電影，各種組合；Apriori 其實是相當慢的演算法，

cues.en: because it just goes through all of these different algorithm or all of these different combinations.
cues.zh: 因為會走遍所有不同的組合。

cues.en: So it says, what if movie one is a good recommendation for movie two or movie one means that person will like movie two, movie one means a person will like movie three, and movie one, movie four,
cues.zh: 它會想：電影一是否適合推薦電影二，或者喜歡電影一的人是否喜歡電影二；喜歡電影一是否喜歡電影三，還有電影一與電影四，

cues.en: and then it actually combines more.
cues.zh: 接著還會組合更多。

cues.en: It says movie one and movie two might mean that person will like movie three and so on.
cues.zh: 例如電影一和電影二，可能表示這個人會喜歡電影三，依此類推。

cues.en: So it actually combines lots and lots and lots of not just pairs, not triplets, it combines four, five, six, seven items in one set and so on.
cues.zh: 它會組合非常多東西，不只是兩個、三個，而是把四、五、六、七個項目放在同一個集合等等。

cues.en: And yeah, so it gets quite big and therefore you need to set some kind of limitations.
cues.zh: 所以規模會變很大，必須設定一些限制。

cues.en: So you need to set a minimum support.
cues.zh: 要設定最低支持度。

cues.en: For instance, you might not want to look at products that have a support of less than 20%.
cues.zh: 例如你可能不想考慮支持度低於 20% 的產品。

cues.en: You might not even want to consider them, because you don't want to waste your time building a model for something that only has a success rate
cues.zh: 甚至完全不想納入，因為不想花時間為一個本身成功率只有

cues.en: of 20% on its own.
cues.zh: 20% 的項目建立模型。

cues.en: Or you might limit it at 5%.
cues.zh: 或者把限制設為 5%。

cues.en: Then you might want to also limit a confidence.
cues.zh: 也可能想限制信賴度。

cues.en: So in our example, the confidence was 17.5%, that somebody who liked one movie will like the other one.
cues.zh: 在我們的例子，喜歡一部電影的人也喜歡另一部的信賴度是 17.5%。

cues.en: Maybe you might want to limit it at anything less than 12%.
cues.zh: 也許你想排除低於 12% 的情況。

cues.en: You don't want to look at it, because it's not as strong enough factor for you, it's not a strong enough rule for you, because there is going to be so many different rules
cues.zh: 不想考慮，因為對你而言這個因素、這條規則不夠強；演算法會輸出非常多不同規則，

cues.en: on the output of this algorithm.
cues.zh: 有很多結果。

cues.en: You already know that you'll have much stronger ones.
cues.zh: 你知道一定會有強得多的規則。

cues.en: So you don't want to consider anything that's less than 12%, or 20%, or whatever percentage you decide to set in that specific scenario.
cues.zh: 因此不考慮低於 12%、20%，或你在特定情境中決定的其他百分比。

cues.en: Then once you've set those, then you take all the subsets in transactions having higher support than minimum support, take all the rules of the subset having higher confidence
cues.zh: 設定好後，取出交易中支持度高於最低支持度的所有子集，再取出其中信賴度高於

cues.en: than minimum confidence, basically apply those two minimums that you've set, and then at the end of course, you sort the rules by the decreasing lift.
cues.zh: 最低信賴度的規則；基本上就是套用這兩個下限，最後當然依提升度由高到低排序。

cues.en: So that's where the lift comes in.
cues.zh: 這時就用到提升度。

cues.en: The rule with the highest lift given these criteria is going to be the strongest rule and that's the one you might want to look into first.
cues.zh: 在符合條件的規則中，提升度最高的會是最強的規則，可能值得優先研究。

cues.en: Something like, I don't know, if a person buys a burger and french fries then they're likely to buy tomato sauce or ketchup as well.
cues.zh: 例如某人買漢堡和薯條，也很可能買番茄醬。

cues.en: And sometimes it makes sense, because you need ketchup to...
cues.zh: 有時這很合理，因為需要番茄醬來……

cues.en: A lot of people like to eat ketchup with their burgers and french fries.
cues.zh: 很多人吃漢堡和薯條時喜歡配番茄醬。

cues.en: So basically, you find the ones with the highest lift and those are the ones on your top 10 or top five and those are the ones that you consider for actually implementing a business decision
cues.zh: 所以找出提升度最高的，列為前十或前五名，再考慮以這些規則作為依據，實際制定商業決策，

cues.en: and basing it on them.
cues.zh: 並以它們為基礎。

cues.en: So that's pretty much how the Apriori algorithm works.
cues.zh: Apriori 演算法大致就是這樣運作。

cues.en: It was quite a long story, I thought we had some good fun here.
cues.zh: 故事很長，希望大家覺得有趣。

cues.en: There was another example that I wanted to share with you.
cues.zh: 還有另一個例子想分享。

cues.en: Oh, okay, so just wanted to mention that recommender systems, things like, companies, like, Amazon use and others and Netflix and so on,
cues.zh: 喔，只是想提到推薦系統，像 Amazon、Netflix 等公司的系統，

cues.en: they would be they would be a good example for using Apriori.
cues.zh: 就是適合使用 Apriori 的例子。

cues.en: Apriori would be good there, but of course, they are much more sophisticated.
cues.zh: Apriori 適用，但當然那些系統複雜得多。

cues.en: They're not just Apriori, they actually use combinations or very specific or specifically designed algorithms.
cues.zh: 不只是 Apriori，而是使用多種組合，或專門設計的特定演算法。

cues.en: So I just don't want you to be confused that Apriori, that means that everything uses a Apriori.
cues.zh: 所以不希望你誤會，覺得所有系統都使用 Apriori。

cues.en: Apriori is just a basic kind of straightforward approach to solving this problem, and it's a good example of how it can be done,
cues.zh: Apriori 只是解決這個問題的基本、直接方式，也是示範如何實作的一個好例子，

cues.en: but of course, there are other ways of doing it.
cues.zh: 但當然還有其他方法。

cues.en: And for instance, we'll look at some of the methods, and in fact, some of the methods that we already use can be used to build recommender systems as well.
cues.zh: 我們也會看一些其他方法，而且有些已經用過的方法，也能用來建立推薦系統。
